evidence.locator: text: Definitions of 'Package', 'Standard Version', and 'Freely Available'; clauses 3-4 and 7 (conditions use alternative source-availability, private-use, naming/manual, Standard-Version, direct-arrangement, and name-connection tests; clause 7 keeps reused parts under this license unless its program-name condition is met, a component/name-dependent scope not expressible as file, library, network, or whole-work)

text: Preamble; Definitions; clauses 1-7 (Package-specific Standard-Version and Freely-Available concepts, multiple disjunctive compliance paths, and the special reuse-and-relicensing rule in clause 7 do not form a conventional permissive or vocabulary-defined copyleft pattern)

text: clauses 1, 3, 4(a), 4(c), and 7 (copyright notices and disclaimers must be duplicated; each changed file needs a prominent how-and-when notice; executable paths can require acquisition instructions, non-standard names, and separate manual-page documentation; reused parts require source attribution, notices, disclaimers, and change marking)

text: clause 1; clause 3 opening and alternatives (a)-(d); clause 4 alternatives (a)-(d); clauses 5 and 7 (duties include preserving copyright/disclaimers, per-file change notices, making modifications Freely Available, supplying machine-readable modified source, Standard-Version executables and acquisition instructions, non-standard names/manual pages, source attribution for reused parts, fee and own-product-advertising limits, or a separate Copyright Holder arrangement; disclose-source and provide-corresponding-source are alternatives, while the vocabulary cannot encode the disjunctions and special duties, represented by unknown)

text: complete-text review, including the Preamble, clauses 1-8 grants and conditions, and clause 9 disclaimer (no express patent grant, patent covenant, patent condition, or patent-claim termination is stated)

text: Preamble; clauses 1-7, especially clauses 2-5 and 7 (use, source and executable distribution, modification, internal organizational use, commercial aggregation, paid support, and commercial sale of generated files support commercial use, distribution, modifications, and private use; clause 7 permits qualifying reused parts to leave this license and bear whatever restrictions the reuser chooses, supporting downstream relicensing/sublicensing; no patent grant is express)

text: clauses 3(c), 4(c), 5, 6 final sentence, 7, 8, and 9 (executable and program-name conditions, copying-fee and Package-fee limits, no own-product advertising, source attribution, and Copyright Holder name-use limits accompany the warranty disclaimer); trademark and warranty capture named categories, but fee, identity, attribution-location, and name-connection restrictions are not losslessly represented, so unknown is retained; no liability limitation is stated

metadata: id=Artistic-dist, name='Artistic License 1.0 (dist)', deprecated=false, osi=false, fsf=false; comments say this variant differs from Artistic-1.0-Perl in clause 7 and clause 5; seeAlso identifies the pinned pexip/os-perl distribution copyright file; text: clauses 3-7 contain alternative compliance paths, fee and naming limits, distribution-specific undump/unexec treatment, and a clause-7 license-scope exit keyed to program-name connection that the vocabulary cannot express losslessly, so this distribution-specific non-OSI variant is not a safe general recommendation

text: clauses 1 and 4-5 (source/executable distribution and aggregation activate conditions); clause 3 (otherwise modifying the Package activates a change notice plus one alternative path); clauses 6-7 (combination/reuse rules depend on undump/unexec treatment, representation as a Standard Version, and whether program names have an immediate connection to the Package); combination, distribution, and modification are captured, while the representation- and name-dependent tests have no exact trigger term and are represented by unknown
